title: Hub retention table (contract 11)
description: What the hub keeps, where, for how long, and whether backups carry it (C-11.9 to C-11.11). One row per record class. A record class with no row is pass-through by default: the hub MUST NOT write it anywhere (C-11.9). The pattern follows web-chat's own one-table rule for caps and retention (web-chat-dev.worktrees/ae-int/lib/server/mirror/retention.js RETENTION, one row per cap with what it protects), but this table is the hub's and describes no web-chat record.

table_version.description: Bumped on any change to a row's class, store, retention or backed_up, and when a row is added, removed or renamed. A change that widens what the hub keeps is a contract change (README rule 7).

rows.description: The record classes, in any order; `record` is unique across rows.

duration.description: An ISO 8601 duration such as P30D, PT10M or P0D.

record.description: The record class's name, as the contract prose uses it (for example activity-entry, queue-message-text).

class.description: 'persist': kept at rest for the retention below. 'held': kept at rest only until an event (delivery, expiry), then deleted. 'transient': in hub memory only, rebuilt after a restart, never written. 'pass-through': relayed or forwarded, never written, held in memory only for one exchange (C-11.9).

content.description: What kind of data the record holds. 'metadata': ids, names, kinds, times, counts, paths the user offered. 'user-text': words a principal wrote that the hub must deliver verbatim. 'derived': content a hub-side daemon built from Read-level relays (dashboards, Home). 'surface-content': pane HTML, params, store, form_state, mirror text, element text. 'bytes': images and documents. 'secret-material': keys, codes, push subscription secrets.

store.description: Where it lives on the hub. 'hub-vm-daemon': a web-chat daemon running on the hub VM (Home, a dashboard), under web-chat's own on-disk rules. 'push-service': handed to a browser vendor's Web Push service, encrypted to the subscription. 'none': nowhere but the wire.

rule.description: 'none': never at rest. 'fixed': `duration` from creation. 'until-event': until `event`, then `after_event` more, and never longer than `max_hold` if the event never comes. 'until-deleted': until its owner (chat, machine, principal, dashboard) is deleted; archive is not deletion. 'external': another system's retention decides (named in `note`).

duration.description: For rule 'fixed': how long from creation.

event.description: For rule 'until-event': the event that starts the end. 'delivered' is the daemon's acceptance of the message as contract 07 acknowledges it, not an upload's ok (C-11.22).

after_event.description: For rule 'until-event': how long the record stays after the event (P0D: deleted at once).

max_hold.description: For rule 'until-event': the longest the record is kept when the event never comes; then it is deleted and the deletion is an Activity entry.

note.description: A short reason or, for 'external', the system whose retention applies.

backed_up.description: Whether the hub's nightly backup carries the record (C-11.24). Always false for 'held' bytes, 'transient' and 'pass-through'.

redaction.description: 'not-applicable': no free text. 'daemon-at-source': the machine's daemon redacted it before it left (mirror text, asks). 'hub-rules': the hub's own redactor ran before the write; for a record whose only words are label or summary fields (chat-event, deny-record), on those fields. 'not-redacted': kept as written, by design (a message Claude must receive verbatim) or by today's web-chat behaviour (pane state on a hub-side daemon); the description says which.

owner_contract.description: The contract whose clauses define the record's shape, or 'hub' for a hub-internal record no cross-side contract defines. This table fixes only residency and retention.

description.description: What the record is and why it is kept this way.
